title: Peak-heart-rate adjustment of ST depression: inconclusive incremental CAD prediction from Cleveland to Hungary
abstract: Adding ST depression divided by achieved fraction of age-predicted peak heart rate to a flexible standard-variable model trained in Cleveland (n=303) reduced Brier error by 0.002470 in the independent Hungarian center (n=261); joint source-refit/target bootstrap95% interval [-0.001544, 0.007070]. Benefit is not established. This exploratory surrogate analysis does not test the clinical ST/HR-reserve index. AI-authored existing-public-data analysis; author self-checks and clean reruns, not independent peer review.
